title: TSMC acquires 0.03% stake in Anthropic for US$500M
content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) said yesterday that its subsidiary TSMC Partners Ltd had acquired 6,024,096 shares in US artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic PBC for about US$500 million.
TSMC Partners paid US$83 per share, the price of Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO), giving TSMC a stake of about 0.03 percent, according to a regulatory filing by the world’s largest contract chipmaker.
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, priced its IPO on Wednesday at a valuation of about US$1.5 trillion. Its shares were scheduled to begin trading on the NASDAQ yesterday under the ticker symbol "ANT."
Photo: AP
The purchase was primarily an equity investment and would be paid for in a lump sum in accordance with Rule 144 of the US Securities Act of 1933, TSMC said.
The purchase follows a Nov. 10 decision by TSMC’s board to authorize investments of up to US$500 million each in Anthropic common shares and preferred shares of OpenAI Group, the developer of ChatGPT.

report.summary: TSMC’s subsidiary bought about 6.02 million Anthropic shares at $83 each, a $500 million stake of roughly 0.03% following Anthropic’s IPO.
report.background: TSMC is the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a key manufacturing partner for advanced AI accelerators. As AI model developers such as Anthropic and OpenAI scale training and inference, demand for leading-edge chips and advanced packaging has surged, making chipmakers central to the AI supply chain. Anthropic, developer of the Claude assistant, has become one of the leading frontier AI labs. Its IPO priced at a reported valuation of about US$1.5 trillion, a landmark for the AI sector. TSMC’s board had authorized up to US$500 million each in Anthropic common shares and OpenAI preferred shares, signaling a strategic-financial interest in the model layer rather than only manufacturing. The purchase was described as primarily an equity investment, paid in a lump sum under Rule 144. The article also notes broader AI supply-chain expansion and TSMC’s tighter China restrictions, underscoring geopolitical and capacity pressures.
key_points: TSMC Partners Ltd acquired 6,024,096 Anthropic shares at US$83 each, roughly US$500 million, giving TSMC about a 0.03% stake. The price matched Anthropic’s IPO price, according to TSMC’s regulatory filing.

Anthropic priced its IPO at a valuation of about US$1.5 trillion and planned to trade on NASDAQ under ticker ANT. The $500 million investment is enormous in absolute terms but tiny in ownership, reflecting Anthropic’s massive valuation.

The purchase follows a Nov. 10 TSMC board decision authorizing up to US$500 million each in Anthropic common shares and OpenAI preferred shares. That suggests TSMC wants financial exposure to two leading AI model developers, not just to chip demand.

TSMC called the purchase primarily an equity investment, paid in a lump sum under Rule 144. Even a passive 0.03% stake signals closer ties between chip manufacturing and frontier AI labs as compute becomes the key bottleneck.
report.impact: The deal blurs the line between chip suppliers and AI model developers. For the AI industry, it reinforces the view that frontier labs are strategic assets and may encourage more cross-investments among chipmakers, cloud providers, and model companies. For developers, Anthropic’s IPO and TSMC’s backing could support Claude API and tooling, but the tiny stake gives TSMC little governance and does not guarantee compute priority. For regular users, the main effect is indirect: more capital for Claude products and competition with ChatGPT, potentially better tools but also concerns about valuation bubbles and concentration of AI power. Watch whether similar chipmaker-lab investments follow.
report.tools: Follow Anthropic’s Claude API, Claude Code, and open Model Context Protocol (MCP) specs; use the Anthropic Cookbook for examples. Track TSMC investor-relations filings and NASDAQ ANT disclosures for stake changes. Compare OpenAI’s API. For open-source experimentation, watch Llama, Mistral, and vLLM for model serving.
